coverage_notes.summary: Twelve targeted searches covered sole/only/last/full-service grocery loss, canceled or suspended emergency food distributions, abrupt pantry or food-bank service closure/reduction, and immediate SNAP/WIC/EBT interruption. No new U.S. event in the bounded window met the qualifying criteria.
coverage_notes.source_priority: Fresh local news, official/provider notices, and direct source pages were prioritized.

degradation.reason: One fresh local-news source page (953 MNC, LaPorte County storm-recovery food distribution) returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch after the search result was retrieved. The available search result described distributions proceeding, not a cancellation; useful coverage remained from the other searches and direct-source opens.

exclusions_observed: Kauaʻi emergency food distributions were scheduled to proceed on October 1 and October 2; a weather cancellation applied to debris pickup, not food distribution.
North Texas reporting concerned flood preparedness and sandbag distribution, not an interruption of food access.
Ohio SNAP reporting concerned administrative cost shifts taking effect October 1, not an immediate interruption of recipient access.
CBS reporting on SNAP work-requirement losses described ongoing policy effects and was published before the bounded window.
Massachusetts EBT theft reporting concerned an individual fraud loss from September 11, not a new official program interruption.
Other results were older, non-U.S., promotional, resilience-focused, or otherwise outside scope.
coverage_notes.production_authority_note: This supplementary recall watch is non-authoritative; production collection remains authoritative.
